papers.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference at datacenter scale is fundamentally bottlenecked by memory capacity and bandwidth limits. Because model weights are read-only and identical across instances, conventional architectures that replicate these parameters across the local DRAM of tens of thousands of accelerators incur massive capital expenditures, significant static power dissipation, and redundant memory-fetch energy. A recent proposal to use optical fiber loops as delay-line memory alleviates these issues, but its recirculating loop must hold the whole model: loop length grows with model size, slack is fixed when the ring is built, and the layouts that serve modern Mixture of Experts (MoE) models efficiently do not fit in it. We propose Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), an open-ended hierarchical Tap-and-Amplify fiber architecture that generalizes and replaces the optical ring paradigm. A centralized memory server continuously broadcasts weights to distributed inference nodes that passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics, delivering parameters directly to compute units without intermediate buffering. To overcome the limitations of continuous weight streaming, we use dynamically-sized slack to accommodate large and variable context lengths. We show how removing the restrictions of the optical ring allows OBM to efficiently serve MoE models. Evaluated at a datacenter scale of 80,000 accelerators, OBM eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system.

papers.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
papers.abstract: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically. Second, FOAM replaces SOAP's dense rotated second moment with a factored Adam-moment estimator based on row-by-column statistics. Under the K-FAC Fisher assumption with a diagonal output curvature, this estimator exactly recovers SOAP's dense second moment, and we measure only a 15-20% K-FAC violation, with negligible effect on the update. Our empirical results support the claim that FOAM matches strong SOAP and Muon baselines in validation loss across scales of large language model (LLM) pre-training, uses half of SOAP's optimizer state, runs at Muon-class wall-clock time, and retains robustness across a three-fold learning-rate range. The results hold from 124M to 760M parameters, demonstrating that SOAP's gains need not require SOAP's cost. Code: https://github.com/naver-ai/foam

digest.summaryZh: FOAM 将 SOAP 简化为输入侧预条件，并以行列统计分解旋转二阶矩，减少状态和特征分解开销，在测试规模保持接近 SOAP/Muon 的验证损失。状态减少不等于整个训练显存减半。
digest.motivationZh: SOAP 等二阶优化器虽改善按步收敛，稠密优化器状态与双侧特征分解增加训练成本。必须确认去掉部分曲率信息后是否仍保留更新质量，且实测墙钟而非只比较迭代步数。优化器状态和矩阵变换会改变训练的内存/算力组成，降低其成本可改善有限设备上的可用规模。与用户的 LLM 训练系统和硬件友好算法有关系，可作为状态压缩与矩阵变换负载研究；不是新的推理芯片。
digest.methodZh: 算法层面的输入单侧预条件，加行乘列的 Adam 二阶矩估计替代 SOAP 的稠密旋转矩。；删除输出侧Kronecker因子及一次特征分解；输入特征基旋转梯度；行列统计重建二阶矩；条件化曲率假设和实证消融；把单侧曲率近似与二阶矩因子化结合，在明确假设下解释近似依据，并验证损失与运行成本的折中。
digest.experimentsZh: 124M、350M、760M LLM 预训练；正文主设置为 FineWeb、8张H100，混合精度训练与各优化器学习率/衰减搜索。 AdamW、Muon、SOAP 等，并分别测验证损失、状态和单步时间。 摘要称 FOAM 接近 SOAP/Muon 验证损失、使用约一半 SOAP 状态，运行时间属于 Muon 量级，并对三倍学习率范围较稳健。正文状态口径为受研究优化器处理的矩阵组，不是总显存。 精确性依赖 K-FAC 与对角输出曲率条件，不能视为任意层无损；主实验规模有限，不能仅凭摘要推广到大规模多十亿模型。状态减少、按步收敛与达标墙钟需要分开比较。

papers.title: Starscream: Reimagining LLM Sharding on AMD Instinct GPUs with GPU Partitioning
papers.abstract: As GPU accelerators grow larger to meet rising compute demands, they exhibit increasingly pronounced non-uniform memory access (NUMA) characteristics that challenge existing LLM frameworks. Chiplet-based architectures provide a practical path to larger GPUs while mitigating manufacturing yield constraints. Modern GPUs such as AMD Instinct MI300X employs such a multi-die design, and further offer GPU partitioning capabilities, partitioning a single physical GPU into multiple logical devices with NUMA-aware memory domains, promising faster kernel launches, and reduced memory access latencies with improved locality. However, current parallelization strategies, designed for homogeneous GPU topologies, when applied under partitioning, extend its unidimensional sharding causing significant performance degradation. Three bottlenecks emerge: (1) memory redundancy; (2) arithmetic intensity collapse; (3) communication overhead from flat collectives. We present Starscream, a rethinking of LLM sharding for the chiplet era. Rather than stretching inter-GPU sharding thinner, Starscream adds intra-GPU sharding along an orthogonal dimension, grounded in three foundational principles: kernel shape preservation, memory redundancy elimination, and communication overhead minimization. These principles form the basis for extending any sharding strategy into the partitioning regime. We demonstrate their effectiveness using tensor parallelism as a case study. On AMD MI300X and MI355X, exploiting partitioning capabilities yields up to 4x speedup for attention and 1.43x for fused GEMMs compared to chiplet-oblivious baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of chiplet-aware designs. Starscream's principles generalize across sharding strategies and future architectures.

digest.summaryZh: Starscream 利用 AMD GPU 分区暴露的 NUMA 域，在物理 GPU 之间保留原分片，在其内部增加正交维度分片，避免 KV 复制、瘦矩阵和扁平通信，让局部访存与计算形状同时受益。
digest.motivationZh: Chiplet GPU 的非均匀访问和分区能力使传统同质 GPU 分片假设失效，逻辑设备变多并不自动带来收益。沿原维度继续细分会复制 KV、降低 GEMM 算术强度并增加通信，抵消局部性好处。局部内存更快只有在张量布局和通信层级相匹配时才有用，分片要兼顾容量、形状与拓扑。高度对应用户的 KV 管理、chiplet存储层次及矩阵核心数据供给研究，可作为真实 GPU 软件协同设计案例。
digest.methodZh: 系统分片与内核协同设计，在 GPU 内选用与 GPU 间不同的维度，同时用层级collective和融合减少搬运。；注意力沿序列维度分布KV；二维GEMM分片保持合适矩阵形状；按GPU内外拓扑分层collective；通过对称内存将计算输出写到目标NUMA区域；把分区当作正交空间维度，而非把跨GPU一维分片继续切细，联合处理算术强度、KV冗余和通信。
digest.experimentsZh: AMD MI300X、MI355X；正文测试代表性注意力decode形状及GEMM/collective形状，涉及GPT-OSS-120B和Llama3模型形状。 忽略chiplet的统一 SPX/NPS1 与朴素分区分片，对照Starscream分片和融合。 摘要报告注意力最高4倍、融合GEMM最高1.43倍。正文说明小batch热点消除收益更强，大batch收益缩小，朴素分片可出现KV复制导致的内存不足。 4倍与1.43倍是特定内核/形状结果，不能直接称完整模型端到端加速；主要详细案例是TP推理，对其他分片策略的普适性需额外验证。代码发布仍是作者计划，本轮未复现。

papers.title: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error-correction (QEC) decoders that achieve low logical error rates under real-time operating constraints. These constraints motivate heuristic decoding algorithms whose error-correction performance must be evaluated through large-scale simulation. High-throughput decoding accelerates this evaluation and the exploration of decoder parameters. Using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) is a natural way to scale these simulations, but naively distributing syndrome batches introduces host-side preprocessing and output-collection overheads that limit scaling. To address these limitations, we extend the Pêlagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder with process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output. We evaluate both one-gross ($[[144,12,12]]$) and two-gross ($[[288,12,18]]$) codes in a multi-GPU environment. Specifically, for the one-gross circuit at $R=50$, eight AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs and eight AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs achieve optimized end-to-end speedups of $5.68\times$ and $6.23\times$, respectively. For the two-gross circuit, the corresponding speedups are $6.92\times$ and $7.01\times$. When throughput is calculated using GPU decoding time, the corresponding two-gross speedups are $7.58\times$ and $7.45\times$, indicating near-linear GPU scaling. We deploy Pêlagos on Lux, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's AMD Instinct MI355X-based supercomputer, as a pathfinding application for high-throughput QEC simulation. This deployment provides a concrete quantum-computing use case for the AI + HPC infrastructure supporting the Genesis Mission's scientific-discovery goals. These end-to-end measurements demonstrate a practical path to accelerating large-scale QEC simulation through efficient multi-GPU decoding.

digest.methodZh: 系统优化为每个 GPU 分配常驻独立进程，CPU线程池准备独立输入，各worker直接写共享输出切片。；初始化前确立GPU设备所有权；并行CPU预处理；共享内存输出避免进程管道大数组序列化；固定每GPU形状和配置缓存；围绕既有解码器重构节点内主机路径，用上下文隔离与输出共享去掉额外扩展障碍。
digest.experimentsZh: one-gross与two-gross码，R=50；8张MI300X或MI355X，每GPU固定syndrome批量并增加总批量。 原单解释器多线程多GPU路径与优化后的单/多GPU吞吐；另分别按端到端和GPU解码时间计时。 8卡one-gross端到端扩展为5.68/6.23倍，two-gross为6.92/7.01倍（MI300X/MI355X）；two-gross只计GPU时间为7.58/7.45倍，不能混称端到端。 固定每GPU工作量的吞吐弱扩展，不是固定任务时延强扩展；本文加速大规模QEC评估，不代表满足实时容错纠错的时延要求。

papers.title: daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving
papers.abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming formal theorem proving. Yet further progress remains constrained by the lack of a transparent and effective data recipe for systematically improving theorem-proving models. In this work, we argue that effective agentic provers require strong mathematical skill priors to ground theorem proving and agentic trajectories to enable long-horizon, interactive proof construction. To this end, we synthesize an agent-native 33.7B-token mid-training corpus covering decomposition, search, self-verification, and revision, together with verifier-grounded agentic trajectories. We further introduce the daVinci-Prover harness, which enables models to construct proofs and interact with a Lean verifier in an isolated workspace, and use it to collect approximately 36K high-quality agent trajectories for supervised fine-tuning. Our mid-training recipe yields an average improvement of 13.7 points over the matched Qwen3-8B SFT-only baseline across MiniF2F, FATE-M, and ProofNet. When applied to the Qwen3.5 series, our approach also yields strong performance across theorem-proving benchmarks and achieves near-saturating MiniF2F performance with memory compaction. The results highlight agent-native mid-training as an effective foundation for developing stronger interactive theorem-proving agents.

papers.title: Fast Serverless LLM Cold Starts by Sharing and Prewarming Startup Work
papers.abstract: When a serverless LLM platform launches a model worker on demand, the cold start lasts roughly a minute, yet only 5-11% of it is spent loading weights. Most of the remainder goes to compilation, memory profiling and runtime setup, which each server performs again even though the outcome is identical across servers or independent of the model. We present Cairn. The server that is first to start a model publishes the weights and engine artifacts to a CXL memory pool shared across the cluster, and the remaining servers read them in place. Model-independent setup is completed ahead of time inside warm containers, and a template process replaces each container as soon as it is used. papers.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
papers.abstract: Remasking allows diffusion language models to revisit generated text, but effective correction requires knowing when and what to revise. Our diagnosis on Sudoku reveals two gaps. Hidden states contain error information that token confidence does not reliably expose, and remasking an isolated error usually reproduces it when the surrounding context remains fixed. These findings motivate DiVR , a verifier that predicts whether a partially generated sequence will reach a correct answer. Trained on the final correctness of the model's own trajectories, DiVR decides when to regenerate a block and which alternative to retain, while the generator itself stays unchanged. On five reasoning benchmarks with LLaDA-8B-Base, DiVR raises the average accuracy of the fine-tuned generator from 35.3\% to 43.4\% at $1.9$-$3.5\times$ the cost of greedy decoding, above search baselines that use $3.8$-$7.4\times$. It also complements post-training such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, and generalizes to other generators, including Dream.

papers.title: Where LLM Agents Get Stuck Debugging Databases: Access More Than Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents are increasingly asked not only to write code but to debug running systems from live runtime data. We report a field observation of one such agent (Claude Code) as it diagnosed eight database incidents in a production message-dispatch engine. In every incident whose root cause depended on runtime concurrency, the agent announced a cause, shipped a fix, and later walked it back, and each wrong guess cost a deploy-and-observe cycle. Mapping each incident to what the agent lacked, we find that access to production state was the most pervasive bottleneck. The missing access included live lock views, untruncated deadlock reports, read-only execution, and an explicit environment context. An access gap was present in all five concurrency-dependent incidents: alone in one, and in four combined with a reasoning error such as anchoring on an early cause, incomplete exploration of the configuration, or a misreading of the code's transaction semantics. The three incidents that did not depend on concurrency needed nothing beyond what the agent already had. Within the incidents, the agent's wrong hypotheses were consistent with the evidence it could see; they were not fabrications. We argue that the next step for production-debugging agents is a forensics layer that gives the agent the access it lacks inside existing security controls. Such a layer would combine a safe interrogation API, a lock-and-deadlock flight recorder, and a production replay harness.
